The members of the board have wanted to exit the console market for a while now, and have been pretty vocal about it. The Xbox division does not bring in the amount of money that investors typically expect from Microsoft, and the amount of money going out in R&D to remain competitive, as well as the marketing dollars to stay relevant in the high-end console race really bit into the revenue that the division does generate.

I doubt it's the end of consoles though, as the ability for those with kids to simply buy a game and know it will work without checking specifications is way too convenient.
